reading.title: Medusa: The Face That Turned to Stone
reading.intro_zh: 本文不复述课文里 Jasper 的停车故事，而是介绍 Jasper 借用的那个真实神话形象——希腊神话中的蛇发女怪美杜莎（Medusa），改写自权威资料 World History Encyclopedia。
passage: In Greek mythology, Medusa was the only mortal among three monstrous sisters known as the Gorgons, the daughters of the ancient sea deities Phorcys and Ceto. Her sisters, Stheno and Euryale, were immortal, yet it is Medusa whose name has endured for nearly three thousand years. Although ancient artists portrayed her variously, sometimes with golden wings, boar-like tusks, or hands of bronze, she is remembered above all for the writhing snakes that replaced her hair and for a gaze so terrible that anyone who looked directly at her face was instantly petrified, frozen forever into lifeless stone.

The Roman poet Ovid offered a tragic explanation for her appearance. According to his account, Medusa had once been a beautiful woman, but after she was violated by the sea god Poseidon inside a sacred temple, the goddess Athena punished her by transforming her hair into a nest of serpents. Her reign of terror ended when the hero Perseus, guided by Athena, refused to meet her eyes directly. Instead, he watched her reflection in a polished bronze shield and beheaded her safely. From her severed head sprang the winged horse Pegasus and the warrior Chrysaor.

Yet Medusa's story did not end with her death, for her power was thought to persist even in her severed head. Perseus presented it to Athena, who fixed it at the centre of her shield to terrify her enemies. The image of the Gorgon's face, called the gorgoneion, then became one of the ancient world's most enduring protective symbols. Greeks and Romans believed it could ward off evil, so they carved it onto temples, armour, and amulets, transforming a creature of horror into a guardian against harm.

questions.question: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How the city of Athens was founded by the goddess Athena.
Why ancient sailors feared the sea deities Phorcys and Ceto.
The myth of Medusa and how her terrifying image became a protective symbol.
The friendship between the hero Perseus and the winged horse Pegasus.
questions.explanation_zh: 全文围绕美杜莎的神话展开：她的身世、被惩罚、被珀尔修斯所杀，以及她的头像后来如何变成驱邪的护身符号，因此主旨是美杜莎的神话及其形象的转变。

questions.question: According to the passage, what made Medusa different from her two sisters?
options: She was the only one of the three Gorgons who could die.
She was the only one born to Phorcys and Ceto.
She was the only one who had snakes instead of hair.
She was the only one who could turn people to stone.
questions.explanation_zh: 文中明确说 Medusa was the only mortal among three monstrous sisters，而她的两个姐妹 Stheno 和 Euryale 是不死的（immortal），所以区别在于只有她会死。

questions.question: How did Perseus manage to kill Medusa without being turned to stone?
options: He attacked her while she was asleep with her eyes closed.
He wore golden wings so he could strike her from above.
He used Athena's shield to hide his own face from her gaze.
He avoided looking at her directly and watched her reflection in a polished shield.
questions.explanation_zh: 文中说珀尔修斯 refused to meet her eyes directly，而是 watched her reflection in a polished bronze shield，因此没有被变成石头，从而能将她斩首。

questions.question: What can be inferred about why the Greeks and Romans carved the gorgoneion onto their temples and armour?
options: They wanted to honour Medusa as a beautiful goddess.
They believed her frightening image could scare away evil and protect them.
They hoped the image would bring Pegasus and Chrysaor back to life.
They were trying to warn travellers that Gorgons lived nearby.
questions.explanation_zh: 文末说人们相信这个形象 could ward off evil，并把它当作 a guardian against harm，由此可推断他们刻它是为了用可怕的形象驱邪、保护自己。

questions.question: In the passage, the word "petrified" most nearly means
options: made extremely curious.
carefully hidden from view.
turned into stone.
filled with sudden anger.
questions.explanation_zh: petrified 在文中与 frozen forever into lifeless stone 并列出现，描述看她的人被瞬间变成石头，所以意思是“变成石头”。

writing.intro_zh: 今天用五个能写出故事感的句式，把 Lesson 28 的现在完成时与强比较结构升级到 B2+ 水平：少见的一类人、持续到现在的麻烦、一次也没成功、毫无效果，以及 one of the... I have ever seen 的强烈主观比较。

patterns.title: one of those rare people who ...
patterns.source: Jasper White is one of those rare people who believes in ancient myths.
patterns.focus_zh: 用这个结构描述“不常见的一类人”，后面接 who 从句说明他特别在哪里。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写一个观念或习惯很少见的人，比如至今仍坚持某种老办法、或对某个原则毫不妥协，后面的 who 从句要抽象、有内容。
must_include: one of those rare people who
patterns.sample: My neighbour is one of those rare people who still believes that a hand-written apology carries more weight than any text message.
patterns.tip_zh: rare people 后面的 who 从句要具体，不要只写 who is nice。

patterns.title: Ever since ..., ...
patterns.source: Ever since he moved in, he has had trouble with cars and their owners.
patterns.focus_zh: ever since 表示“从那时起一直到现在”，很适合写一个持续的问题。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写自从某项制度、规则或环境发生变化以后，一个问题不断累积、持续到现在，后半句用现在完成时体现延续性。
patterns.sample: Ever since the new gate code was introduced, delivery drivers have repeatedly left parcels in the wrong building, and complaints have steadily multiplied.
patterns.tip_zh: 后半句最好用现在完成时或现在完成进行时，体现“到现在还有关联”。

patterns.title: has not been able to ... even once
patterns.source: He has not been able to get his own car into his garage even once.
patterns.focus_zh: 这个结构强调反复尝试却一次也没成功，情绪比 simply cannot 更强。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写某人尽管努力或付出代价，却因为被阻挠、规则不清或外部干扰，一次也没能完成某件本该理所当然的事。
patterns.sample: Despite renting the space for half a year, she has not been able to leave her car there overnight even once, because strangers keep occupying it.
patterns.tip_zh: even once 放在句尾，能把“从来没有成功过”的感觉压出来。

patterns.title: have not had any effect
patterns.source: These have not had any effect.
patterns.focus_zh: have not had any effect 用来说明某个办法看起来有用，但实际上没有改变结果。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写一个看起来合理的提醒、规定或劝告，对某一群人毫无作用，effect 后面用 on 指明对象。
patterns.sample: The polite reminders the management posted in every stairwell have not had any effect on the residents who block the fire lane each morning.
patterns.tip_zh: effect 后面可以接 on someone，说明“对谁没有起作用”。

patterns.title: one of the ... I have ever seen
patterns.source: It is one of the ugliest faces I have ever seen.
patterns.focus_zh: one of the... I have ever seen 是强比较，表示“我见过的最……之一”。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写一个你印象最深的标志或装置——最清楚、最荒谬、最没用或最巧妙的之一，用最高级加上 I have ever seen 表达强烈主观评价。
patterns.sample: Honestly, that overgrown, half-faded warning board is one of the most useless public signs I have ever seen in this entire neighbourhood.
patterns.tip_zh: the 后面要用最高级，比如 clearest, strangest, funniest, ugliest。
